result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_independent_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a set of nodes forms an independent set. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L27014-L27093){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_independent_set(nodes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is independent set](/assets/graphs/is-independent-set.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same two-by-three ladder on both sides, with the candidate nodes outlined. Left: A, C, E share no edge, so is_independent_set() returns True. Right: A, C, F, where the edge between C and F (shown in the accent color) joins two members, so is_independent_set() returns False." width="100%"} An independent set (also called a stable set) is a set of vertices in a graph where no two vertices are adjacent. This method validates whether the given nodes satisfy this property. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs to check. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the nodes form a valid independent set (no edges between them), `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} An independent set contains no adjacent vertices, so validation reduces to scanning the input set for any pair joined by an edge: a single such edge witnesses invalidity. The cost is $O(|V| + |E|)$ in the worst case, or $O(|S|^2)$ in the neighbor-set variant when $|S|$ is small. Empty and singleton sets pass trivially. The dual property, that the *complement* of an independent set is a *vertex cover*, is what ties this validation to some of the most well-studied problems in combinatorial optimization. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a path `A-B-C-D`, `A` and `C` are not directly connected, so they form a valid independent set: ::: {#15684cea .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") c_id = graph.get_id_from_label("C") # Returns True graph.is_independent_set([a_id, c_id]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Adding `D` breaks it, since `C` and `D` are adjacent: ::: {#7fe8789c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} d_id = graph.get_id_from_label("D") # Returns False graph.is_independent_set([a_id, c_id, d_id]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: This is a handy way to confirm that a computed independent set is actually valid: ::: {#4ead7ad3 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(10) mis = graph.maximal_independent_set(seed=23) # Returns True: maximal_independent_set() always produces a valid result graph.is_independent_set(mis) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
